biography: Sam Hancock, a name synonymous with audacious speed and a touch of British flamboyance, hails from the unassuming town of Market Deeping. Unlike many racing prodigies born into motorsport dynasties, Sam's journey began with a battered go-kart salvaged from a local scrapyard. Hours spent tinkering in his father's garage, fueled by dreams of Le Mans glory, transformed that rusty kart into a formidable machine, dominating local karting circuits. His breakthrough came at the age of 18, during a support race at Silverstone. A daring last-lap overtake, executed with the precision of a seasoned veteran, caught the eye of Lola's junior team manager. From there, his ascent was meteoric. Now, at the peak of his career, Hancock is a force to be reckoned with in the world of endurance racing, piloting the Lola B05/40 Turbo with his signature blend of controlled aggression and raw talent, constantly pushing the boundaries of both himself and his machine. He is known to relish the pressure of being in the spotlight, often seen joking with the pit crew just moments before the start of a race, a testament to his unflappable confidence.
drivingStyle: Hancock's driving style is best described as 'calculated chaos'. He possesses an uncanny ability to extract maximum performance from his car while maintaining a level of control that borders on the miraculous. He is known for his late-braking maneuvers and aggressive corner entries, often carrying more speed into the apex than seems humanly possible. Tire management isn't always his strong suit, as he tends to push the rubber to its absolute limit, but his sheer pace often compensates for any strategic disadvantages. Under pressure, Hancock thrives; the more intense the situation, the cooler and more focused he becomes, a trait that has earned him a reputation as a clutch performer.

rivalries.reason: A long-standing rivalry fueled by contrasting driving styles and national pride. Dubois, a meticulous strategist, often clashes with Hancock's more impulsive approach.

Their battles on track are legendary, marked by aggressive overtaking and near-miss collisions. The tension extends beyond the circuit, with both drivers frequently engaging in verbal sparring during press conferences.

Tanaka and Hancock have been fierce competitors since their karting days. A controversial incident at the Suzuka 1000km, where Hancock allegedly forced Tanaka off the track, ignited a bitter feud that continues to this day.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky pair of socks, featuring a Union Jack pattern, during every race weekend.
Listens to a specific playlist of classic rock anthems before each race to get himself 'in the zone'.
Has a habit of polishing his helmet visor obsessively, even when it's already spotless.
famousQuote: Second place is just the first loser. I'm here to win, and I'll do whatever it takes to get there... within reason, of course.
careerHighlight: Winning the 24 Hours of Daytona in 2028 alongside his teammates after starting from the back of the grid due to a pre-race mechanical issue, demonstrating his remarkable ability to overcome adversity.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2029 with only two hours remaining, costing his team a guaranteed victory and leaving him devastated.
